questions.question: Trace the chain of causes and consequences of rural depopulation, and give two strategies used to slow it.
questions.expected_answer: Push factors such as drought, farm mechanisation shedding labour, degraded land and thin services drive people out, while pull factors like wages, schools and hospitals draw them to the cities. The young and skilled leave first, so the remaining population ages; schools and clinics close as numbers fall; farm labour dries up; and local businesses fail because their threshold populations have left. Strategies include rural development projects and agri-processing that create local jobs, improved roads and services, and land reform through restitution, redistribution and tenure reform.

questions.question: Describe the layout of the South African city model and explain how its apartheid origins produce today's urban issues.
questions.expected_answer: The South African city keeps a central business district at its core, with the formerly white suburbs holding the well-serviced middle ground, a transition zone of aging mixed land use around the core, and townships and informal settlements pressed to the far periphery behind deliberately planned buffer strips of open land. Because homes were placed far from workplaces, residents carry long, costly commutes, while the periphery bears housing shortages, service backlogs and growing informal settlements. Strategies worth naming are in-situ upgrading of informal settlements, investment in public transport such as bus rapid transit, and inner-city renewal.

questions.question: Name South Africa's four core industrial regions, and distinguish an Industrial Development Zone from a Spatial Development Initiative with one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: The four core regions are Gauteng (the PWV), Durban-Pinetown, Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage and the South-western Cape. An Industrial Development Zone is a purpose-built industrial estate tied to a port or airport and designed to attract export-oriented manufacturing — Coega is the flagship example. A Spatial Development Initiative is a corridor of coordinated investment linking regions to unlock economic potential — the Maputo Corridor running from Gauteng to the neighbouring harbour at Maputo is the classic example.
